title: Fractions
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 3; not yet checked by a Kenyan maths teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Outcomes a and b are KICD's words, but the PDF's text layer lost the fraction symbols: from the learning experiences they are 1/2, 1/4 and 1/8 (to confirm by a person). c is attitudinal.

skills.key_step: The child checks the parts are equal, counts them, and names one part by how many make the whole.

floor.prerequisite: Halves and quarters of a whole (Grade 2).
floor.question: A circle folded into 2 equal parts: what is one part?

steps: How many parts make the whole?
One part is one of that many.
Write 1 over the number of parts.
contexts: cutting a cake at a birthday

board.do: Draw a rectangle in 8 equal parts; shade one.

misconceptions.repair: No: a half needs two equal parts.

misconceptions.ask: How many equal parts make the whole?
How many parts do you see when you unfold it?

checks.question: A circle in 4 equal parts, 1 shaded. What fraction is shaded?
Is a square cut into 2 unequal parts in halves?

skills.key_step: The child says more equal parts of the same whole make each part smaller.

floor.question: A circle in 8 equal parts: one part is?

board.do: Draw three same bars in 2, 4 and 8 parts.
Point at one part of each.

misconceptions.ask: Which piece would you rather have?
misconceptions.repair: The half: fewer pieces make bigger pieces.

misconceptions.ask: Are the watermelon and the orange the same size?
misconceptions.repair: No, so the half is not always bigger.

misconceptions.ask: Which strip has the smallest piece?
How many pieces does the quarter become?

checks.question: Which is smaller, 1/4 or 1/8 of the same bread?

skills.key_step: The child shares the group into that many equal groups and counts one group.
steps: How many equal groups? The bottom number.

board.do: The child shares the dots one by one into the rings.
Wait for the count in one ring.

misconceptions.ask: How many oranges on one plate?
How many in each of the 2 groups?
Do all heaps have the same number?
misconceptions.repair: No, so it is not a quarter.

misconceptions.ask: Is an eighth of 16 more or less than 16?
